message: No detected input validation: The code only checks `len(book_id.text) is not 0` and `not('fail_message' in book_reviews)`, but performs no schema, type, range, or structural validation on the ISBN input or the scraped review data.

No detected untrusted source handling: Data is fetched from the Goodreads API and scraped from external URLs with no checksum verification, signature validation, pinned revisions, or authentication of the remote source.
No detected label flipping detection: There is no code that validates label values, compares label distributions, or uses any label-noise detection tool before or during training.
No detected data poisoning defenses: No outlier detection, statistical anomaly checks, or filtering of suspicious training samples is performed anywhere in the data preparation pipeline.

No detected model integrity verification: The code loads pretrained weights via polarity_lstm.load_weights('./model/model_lstm.hdf5') and vector files without any hash check, signature verification, or pinned revision check.

No detected label distribution validation: The train() function in lstm.py reads labels and converts them with to_categorical but performs no class balance check, expected-label-set validation, or anomaly detection on the training samples.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no neural-cleanse-style trigger detection, activation-pattern analysis, or gradient anomaly detection anywhere in the training pipeline.
No detected differential privacy: No differential privacy libraries (Opacus, TensorFlow Privacy, DP-SGD) or related mechanisms are imported or used in any part of the training code.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: There is no use of adversarial attack frameworks (Foolbox, ART, FGSM, PGD) or any robustness stress testing anywhere in the code.

No detected metric tampering protection: There is no held-out test set isolation, hashing/signing of evaluation data, or use of multiple independent metrics to guard against metric manipulation; the code simply runs inference and computes scores without any such controls.

No detected input sanitization: The ISBN string from the URL path is passed directly to external API calls and scraped text is fed into the model pipeline without any shape, range, or schema validation.

No detected output bounds checks: The model's raw output arrays are processed with np.argmax via find_max() with no NaN guards, probability sanity checks, or confidence threshold filtering before being returned.
No detected prompt injection defenses: This is not an LLM-based inference pipeline (it uses LSTM and Word2Vec models), so prompt injection defenses are not applicable and none are implemented.
